key_insight: Learn a convex, frame-indifferent dissipation potential instead of the constitutive law directly, so the resulting PDE remains well-posed while still fitting velocity-only data.
engineering_relevance: This gives a safer way to identify material behavior in solid/fluid mechanics from indirect measurements, with better stability and transfer to unseen geometries.
method: Use an input-convex neural network potential (ICNNE) to enforce convexity by design.
Symmetrize the input to guarantee frame-indifference and evenness in the second strain-rate invariant.
Add a penalty that drives the potential gradient to zero at the origin, promoting dissipativity.
evidence_signal: The approach is tested on four benchmarks—compressible Navier-Stokes, Herschel-Bulkley flow, Hibler sea-ice rheology, and DEM data—and is reported to recover known physics, generalize to unseen geometries, and remain stable where unstructured methods fail.
watch_item: Training depends on coupled FEM/NN optimization and a dissipation penalty, so performance may be sensitive to implementation details, numerical resolution, and penalty weighting.
paper_title: Well-posed by Design: Learning Constitutive Laws from Velocity Data using Convex Neural Network Potentials
